arguments.premise_synthesis: Within a fixed money supply, fluctuations in the savings pool determine interest rates: a large savings pool drives rates down, encouraging borrowing and investment, while a depleted savings pool pushes rates up, encouraging saving and lending. This self-regulating mechanism prevents the massive boom-bust cycles that occur when central banks artificially distort rates.
arguments.conclusion_supported: Under a fixed money supply, interest rates self-regulate to balance saving and spending, thereby avoiding boom-bust cycles.
